newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq gives new oil pricing formula to U.N..
newsitem.headline: Iraq gives new oil pricing formula to U.N..

text.p: Iraq has submitted its oil pricing formula for the month of November to the United Nations, U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa said.

She said the formula, which determines prices for the still-pending oil-for-food plan, was sent to the United Nations on Thursday and then given to three oil experts or overseers for their comments. After that it will be considered by the Security Council's sanctions committee, she said.

The last pricing formula was submitted in August and approved by all members of the committee except the United States. Iraq recently said it would not agree to implementation of the oil-for-food plan until the pricing mechanism was approved by the committee.

At issue is an arrangement that allows Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil over six months, on a renewable basis, to buy food, medicine and other necessities to help offset the impact on ordinary Iraqis of sanctions imposed after Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
An agreed-on pricing plan would prevent individual contracts from going through the committee and allow the overseers from the United States, Norway and Russia, to approve contracts.

Diplomats said that Iraqi envoys as well as some members of the committee believe that Washington wanted the ability to stop the deal at any point by forcing each contract to go through the full committee where any one member can oppose a decision.

Arrangements to launch the plan were close to completion when Iraqi President Saddam Hussein sent troops into the largely Kurdish-inhabited north of the country at the end of August to back one side in an inter-Kurdish conflict.
Since then Iraq has told the United Nations it would decide which local staff worked with the United Nations and restrict the movement of U.N. personnel in the north.
Both demands are unacceptable but the diplomats said Iraqi officials appeared hopeful these issues could be resolved if the pricing formula controversy were settled.
